correctness.rationale: Pauli commutators give the 3x3 Bloch generator M with initial z=1. At b=0 the y,z-plane is damped rotation and at a=0 z obeys the classical scalar equation. For ab≠0 the symmetric part of N=M+2γI is diag(4γ,0,0), and its eigenvector equations force first component nonzero; all eigenvalues of N have positive real part. Analogously M has strictly negative real spectrum. Hence e^(2γt)z(t), a nonzero exponential polynomial with all exponents of positive real parts, is unbounded in absolute value; its leading finite trigonometric polynomial has positive mean square. Taylor gives z(t)-e^(-2γt)=-2a²t²+O(t³). The exact Laplace resolvent P_b(s),Q_b(s) and simple pole at zero at b=0 give λ_s=-2γb²/(γ²+a²)+O(b⁴) and A_s=a²b²/(γ²+a²)²+O(b⁴). Independently checked numerical matrix exponentials for several real a,b,γ and eigenspectrum in the off-axis case; finite tests corroborate rather than prove universal spectral argument.
